"""Solved local stochastic HANK policies with conservative distribution reduction.

This is a first-order rational-expectations solution around a heterogeneous
steady state, not a global aggregate-risk or second-order welfare calculation.
The full household marginal values remain controls in the Schur system.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.linalg import null_space, ordqz, solve, solve_discrete_lyapunov
from scipy.optimize import root

from ._hank_one_asset_recursive import _OneAssetKernel

__all__ = ["HANKDistributionBasis", "StochasticHANKPolicy", "HANKStochasticResult", "HANKStochasticTreeResult",
           "solve_hank_stochastic_policy", "solve_hank_stochastic_tree"]


def _array(value, name, shape=None):
    if np.iscomplexobj(value):
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be finite and real")
    out = np.array(value, dtype=float, copy=True)
    if not np.isfinite(out).all() or (shape is not None and out.shape != shape):
        raise ValueError(f"invalid shape or nonfinite {name}")
    return out


def _integer(value, name, minimum=1):
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, np.integer)) or value < minimum:
        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be an integer >= {minimum}")
    return int(value)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HANKDistributionBasis:
    """Orthonormal mass/moment-preserving directions around a fixed distribution.

    Linear reconstructions can be negative outside a local neighborhood. They
    are never clipped or renormalized; ``decode`` raises by default. ``encode``
    checks the model's exact marginal/moment restrictions before projection.
    """
    center: np.ndarray
    vectors: np.ndarray
    constraints: np.ndarray
    diagnostics: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        d = _array(self.center, "center")
        B, C = _array(self.vectors, "vectors"), _array(self.constraints, "constraints")
        if (d.ndim < 1 or np.min(d) < 0 or abs(d.sum()-1) > 1e-10 or B.ndim != 2
                or C.ndim != 2 or B.shape[0] != d.size or C.shape[0] != d.size or B.shape[1] < 1):
            raise ValueError("invalid distribution basis dimensions or probability mass")
        if (not np.allclose(B.T@B, np.eye(B.shape[1]), atol=1e-10, rtol=0)
                or np.max(abs(C.T@B)) > 1e-9 or np.max(abs(B.sum(axis=0))) > 1e-9):
            raise ValueError("basis must be orthonormal and preserve mass and constraints")
        for name, value in (("center", d), ("vectors", B), ("constraints", C)):
            value.flags.writeable = False
            object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
        object.__setattr__(self, "diagnostics", dict(self.diagnostics))

    @property
    def rank(self) -> int:
        return int(self.vectors.shape[1])

    def project(self, difference: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Project a signed distribution difference; no positivity assumption."""
        return self.vectors.T @ _array(difference, "difference", self.center.shape).ravel()

    def encode(self, distribution: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        d = _array(distribution, "distribution", self.center.shape)
        delta = d.ravel()-self.center.ravel()
        if np.min(d) < -1e-12 or abs(d.sum()-1) > 1e-10:
            raise ValueError("distribution must be a probability measure")
        if np.max(abs(self.constraints.T@delta)) > 1e-9:
            raise ValueError("distribution violates fixed income marginals or asset-market restrictions")
        return self.vectors.T@delta

    def decode(self, coefficients: np.ndarray, *, check_positive: bool = True) -> np.ndarray:
        c = _array(coefficients, "coefficients", (self.rank,))
        d = self.center + (self.vectors@c).reshape(self.center.shape)
        if check_positive and d.min() < -1e-12:
            raise ValueError("compressed distribution is negative; reduce the excursion or enrich the basis")
        return d


def _make_basis(kernel, rank, snapshots=None):
    C = kernel.constraints
    C = C / np.linalg.norm(C, axis=0)
    Q, _ = np.linalg.qr(C, mode="reduced")
    maximum = kernel.d.size - Q.shape[1]
    if rank is None:
        B = null_space(Q.T)
        return HANKDistributionBasis(kernel.d, B, Q, dict(method="full_constraint_nullspace", rank=maximum))
    rank = _integer(rank, "distribution_rank")
    if rank > maximum:
        raise ValueError(f"distribution_rank exceeds the constrained dimension {maximum}")
    if snapshots is None:
        seed = kernel.seed_directions()
        columns = []
        for _ in range(max(24, 3*rank)):
            seed -= Q@(Q.T@seed)
            columns.append(seed.copy())
            seed = np.column_stack([kernel.fixed_forward(v) for v in seed.T])
        candidates = np.column_stack(columns)
        method = "projected_transport_krylov"
    else:
        data = _array(snapshots, "snapshots")
        if data.ndim != kernel.d.ndim+1 or data.shape[1:] != kernel.d.shape:
            raise ValueError("snapshots must have shape (observations, *distribution.shape)")
        if np.min(data) < -1e-12 or np.max(abs(data.reshape(len(data), -1).sum(axis=1)-1)) > 1e-10:
            raise ValueError("snapshots must contain probability distributions")
        candidates = (data-kernel.d).reshape(len(data), -1).T
        if np.max(abs(Q.T@candidates)) > 1e-9:
            raise ValueError("snapshots violate fixed distribution constraints")
        method = "snapshot_svd"
    candidates -= Q@(Q.T@candidates)
    U, singular, _ = np.linalg.svd(candidates, full_matrices=False)
    available = int(np.sum(singular > (singular[0] if len(singular) else 1)*1e-13))
    if available < rank:
        raise ValueError(f"only {available} independent distribution directions; lower distribution_rank")
    # Reproject and orthogonalize to control cancellation in low-energy vectors.
    B, _ = np.linalg.qr(U[:, :rank]-Q@(Q.T@U[:, :rank]), mode="reduced")
    omitted = np.linalg.norm(candidates-B@(B.T@candidates))/max(np.linalg.norm(candidates), 1e-300)
    return HANKDistributionBasis(kernel.d, B, Q, dict(method=method, rank=rank,
        available_directions=available, training_relative_error=float(omitted),
        singular_values=singular.tolist()))


@dataclass
class HANKStochasticResult:
    """History paths and diagnostics, with local approximation scope explicit."""
    paths: pd.DataFrame
    states: np.ndarray
    distributions: np.ndarray
    diagnostics: dict[str, Any]
    converged: bool


@dataclass
class HANKStochasticTreeResult:
    """Nonlinear finite histories and a first-order stochastic continuation."""
    nodes: pd.DataFrame
    paths: pd.DataFrame
    distributions: np.ndarray
    policies: dict[str, np.ndarray]
    terminal_states: np.ndarray
    converged: bool
    diagnostics: dict[str, Any]
    metadata: dict[str, Any]

    def to_dataframe(self):
        return self.nodes.join(self.paths)


@dataclass
class StochasticHANKPolicy:
    """Stable infinite-horizon policy y=Gx, x_next=Hx+innovation.

    States are distribution coefficients, inherited nominal-rate deviation,
    and the current AR(1) monetary disturbance. Controls are household marginal
    values followed by aggregate log coordinates. Future innovations have zero
    conditional mean and standard deviation ``shock_std``; first-order policy
    coefficients are certainty equivalent. No precautionary shift is implied.
    """
    basis: HANKDistributionBasis
    transition: np.ndarray
    feedback: np.ndarray
    rho: float
    shock_std: float
    diagnostics: dict[str, Any]
    _kernel: Any = field(repr=False)
    _F0: np.ndarray = field(repr=False)
    _F1: np.ndarray = field(repr=False)

    @property
    def converged(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.diagnostics["equilibrium_residual_max_abs"] < 1e-8)

    @property
    def steady_state(self):
        from copy import deepcopy
        return deepcopy(self._kernel.ss)

    @property
    def aggregate_feedback(self) -> np.ndarray:
        return self.feedback[-len(self._kernel.aggregate_names):].copy()

    def state(self, distribution: np.ndarray | None = None, *, lag_nominal: float = 0.,
              monetary_shock: float = 0.) -> np.ndarray:
        d = self.basis.center if distribution is None else distribution
        return np.r_[self.basis.encode(d), _array([lag_nominal, monetary_shock], "aggregate states", (2,))]

    def covariance(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """First-order unconditional covariance; does not shift steady-state means."""
        Q = np.zeros_like(self.transition)
        Q[-1, -1] = self.shock_std**2
        return solve_discrete_lyapunov(self.transition, Q)

    def simulate(self, innovations: np.ndarray, *, initial_state: np.ndarray | None = None) -> HANKStochasticResult:
        """Simulate the solved linear system; report signed reconstruction limits."""
        eps = _array(innovations, "innovations")
        if eps.ndim != 1 or not len(eps):
            raise ValueError("innovations must be a nonempty vector")
        ns, k = len(self.transition), self.basis.rank
        x = np.zeros(ns) if initial_state is None else _array(initial_state, "initial_state", (ns,))
        states, distributions, rows = [], [], []
        error = 0.
        for innovation in eps:
            x[-1] += innovation
            y, xp = self.feedback@x, self.transition@x
            vec, nxt = np.r_[x, y], np.r_[xp, self.feedback@xp]
            error = max(error, float(np.max(abs(self._F0@vec+self._F1@nxt))))
            rows.append(dict(zip(self._kernel.aggregate_names, y[-len(self._kernel.aggregate_names):])))
            states.append(x.copy())
            distributions.append(self.basis.decode(x[:k], check_positive=False))
            x = xp
        dist = np.asarray(distributions)
        return HANKStochasticResult(pd.DataFrame(rows), np.asarray(states), dist,
            dict(scope="local first-order stochastic equilibrium; aggregate paths are log deviations",
                 linear_equilibrium_error=error, minimum_reconstructed_mass=float(dist.min()),
                 negative_reconstructed_mass=float(np.maximum(-dist, 0).sum(axis=tuple(range(1, dist.ndim))).max()),
                 stochastic_tail_solved=True, distribution_rank=k), error < 1e-8)

    def _forecast(self, next_state, nominal):
        kernel = self._kernel
        nm = len(kernel.m)
        expected = kernel.m + self.feedback[:nm]@next_state
        if np.min(expected) <= 0:
            raise ValueError("terminal household marginal value left the positive domain")
        branches = []
        for innovation in (-self.shock_std, self.shock_std):
            x = next_state.copy()
            x[-1] += innovation
            if np.min(kernel.m+self.feedback[:nm]@x) <= 0:
                raise ValueError("a terminal shock branch has nonpositive household marginal values")
            u = self.aggregate_feedback@x
            pi, Y = np.expm1(u[0]), kernel.Y*np.exp(u[2])
            gross = (1+nominal)/(1+pi)
            if not np.isfinite([pi, Y, gross]).all() or min(Y, gross) <= 0:
                raise ValueError("terminal aggregate policy left its local domain")
            branches.append((.5, Y, u[0], gross))
        return expected, branches

    def audit(self, innovations: np.ndarray, *, tolerance: float = 1e-5) -> HANKStochasticResult:
        """Held-out full-distribution nonlinear rollout of the local policy.

        Each period solves continuation/transport consistency with the full
        household grid. Aggregate policy coefficients stay fixed. Market and
        goods errors therefore measure approximation error rather than a refit.
        Euler/KKT errors include household interpolation error and are reported
        separately; they are not hidden by the aggregate acceptance threshold.
        """
        eps = _array(innovations, "innovations")
        if eps.ndim != 1 or not len(eps) or not np.isfinite(tolerance) or tolerance <= 0:
            raise ValueError("nonempty innovations and a positive finite tolerance are required")
        kernel, k = self._kernel, self.basis.rank
        d = kernel.d.copy()
        lag = shock = error = compression = budget = euler = exit_mass = 0.
        rows, states, distributions, statuses = [], [], [], []
        for innovation in eps:
            shock = self.rho*shock + innovation
            # Actual transported distributions need not satisfy the asset-market
            # restriction exactly when a local policy has nonlinear residuals.
            x = np.r_[self.basis.project(d-self.basis.center), lag, shock]
            u = self.aggregate_feedback@x
            prices = kernel.prices(u, lag, shock, distribution=d)

            def evaluate(z):
                xp = np.r_[z, prices["nominal"]-kernel.r, self.rho*shock]
                expected, branches = self._forecast(xp, prices["nominal"])
                h = kernel.backward(expected, prices)
                dp = kernel.forward(d, h)
                return z-self.basis.project(dp-self.basis.center), h, dp, expected, branches

            fit = root(lambda z: evaluate(z)[0], (self.transition@x)[:k], tol=1e-10)
            consistency, h, dp, expected, branches = evaluate(fit.x)
            consistency_error = float(np.max(abs(consistency)))
            statuses.append(dict(success=bool(consistency_error < 1e-9), message=str(fit.message)))
            continuation = sum(prob*Y/prices["Y"]*logpi/gross for prob, Y, logpi, gross in branches)
            residual, row = kernel.markets(d, h, prices, continuation)
            checks = kernel.household_checks(d, h, prices, expected)
            projection = self.basis.decode(self.basis.project(dp-self.basis.center), check_positive=False)
            gap = float(np.sum(abs(dp-projection)))
            error = max(error, float(np.max(abs(residual))), abs(row["goods_mkt"]), consistency_error)
            compression = max(compression, gap)
            budget, euler = max(budget, checks["budget_error"]), max(euler, checks["euler_kkt_max"])
            exit_mass = max(exit_mass, checks["grid_exit_mass"])
            row.update(compression_l1=gap, continuation_error=consistency_error,
                       euler_kkt_max=checks["euler_kkt_max"], shock=shock)
            rows.append(row)
            states.append(x)
            distributions.append(d.copy())
            d, lag = dp, prices["nominal"]-kernel.r
        dist = np.asarray([*distributions, d])
        mass_error = float(np.max(abs(dist.reshape(len(dist), -1).sum(axis=1)-1)))
        ok = bool(error <= tolerance and budget < 1e-8 and mass_error < 1e-10
                  and dist.min() >= -1e-12 and exit_mass < 1e-10 and all(s["success"] for s in statuses))
        return HANKStochasticResult(pd.DataFrame(rows), np.asarray(states), dist,
            dict(scope="nonlinear full-distribution audit of fixed local stochastic policy",
                 market_residual_max_abs=error, compression_l1_max=compression, mass_error=mass_error,
                 minimum_mass=float(dist.min()), household_budget_error=budget, euler_kkt_max=euler,
                 policy_grid_exit_mass=exit_mass, tolerance=tolerance, continuation_solves=statuses), ok)


def solve_hank_stochastic_policy(steady_state: Any, *, distribution_rank: int | None = 12,
                                 snapshots: np.ndarray | None = None, rho: float = .7,
                                 shock_std: float = .0001, max_system_size: int = 1800) -> StochasticHANKPolicy:
    """Solve a reduced-state local rational-expectations equilibrium by ordered QZ.

    ``distribution_rank=None`` retains the full constrained distribution and is
    an independent compression check. Snapshots, when supplied, train the basis
    only; policy coefficients always solve household and equilibrium equations.
    Dense QZ retains all household marginal values, so ``max_system_size``
    bounds its dimension, not RSS. A unit root, incorrect stable-root count or
    singular state projection raises explicitly. No regularized policy is used.
    """
    if not np.isfinite([rho, shock_std]).all() or abs(rho) >= 1 or shock_std < 0:
        raise ValueError("require abs(rho) < 1 and nonnegative finite shock_std")
    limit = _integer(max_system_size, "max_system_size")
    from .one_asset_hank import OneAssetHANKSteadyState
    kernel: Any
    if isinstance(steady_state, OneAssetHANKSteadyState):
        kernel = _OneAssetKernel(steady_state)
    else:
        from .hank_two_asset_equilibrium import _TwoAssetKernel
        kernel = _TwoAssetKernel(steady_state)
    requested = (kernel.d.size-kernel.constraints.shape[1] if distribution_rank is None
                 else _integer(distribution_rank, "distribution_rank"))
    anticipated = requested+2+len(kernel.m)+len(kernel.aggregate_names)
    if anticipated > limit:
        raise ValueError(f"Schur system dimension {anticipated} exceeds max_system_size={limit}")
    zero_prices = kernel.prices(np.zeros(len(kernel.aggregate_names)), 0., 0., distribution=kernel.d)
    zero_household = kernel.backward(kernel.m, zero_prices)
    zero_residual, zero_accounts = kernel.markets(kernel.d, zero_household, zero_prices, 0.)
    base_error = max(float(np.max(abs(zero_residual))), abs(zero_accounts["goods_mkt"]),
        float(np.max(abs(zero_household["m"]-kernel.m)/(1+abs(kernel.m)))),
        float(np.max(abs(kernel.forward(kernel.d, zero_household)-kernel.d))))
    if (not np.isfinite(base_error) or base_error > 1e-8 or np.min(kernel.d) < -1e-12
            or abs(kernel.d.sum()-1) > 1e-10 or np.min(kernel.m) <= 0):
        raise ValueError("steady-state equations or distribution are inconsistent")
    basis = _make_basis(kernel, distribution_rank, snapshots)
    ns = basis.rank+2
    dim = ns+len(kernel.m)+len(kernel.aggregate_names)
    if dim > limit:
        raise ValueError(f"Schur system dimension {dim} exceeds max_system_size={limit}")
    eye, zero = np.eye(dim), np.zeros(dim)
    F0 = np.column_stack([kernel.linear_residual(v, zero, basis, rho) for v in eye])
    F1 = np.column_stack([kernel.linear_residual(zero, v, basis, rho) for v in eye])
    S, T, alpha, beta, _, Z = ordqz(-F0, F1, sort="iuc", output="complex")
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        eigen = alpha/beta
    modulus = abs(eigen)
    if np.any(abs(modulus-1) < 1e-8) or int(np.sum(modulus < 1-1e-8)) != ns:
        raise ValueError(f"stochastic equilibrium fails determinacy: {np.sum(modulus < 1-1e-8)} stable roots for {ns} states")
    Zx = Z[:ns, :ns]
    condition = float(np.linalg.cond(Zx))
    if not np.isfinite(condition) or condition > 1e12:
        raise ValueError("stable Schur subspace does not identify a well-conditioned state policy")
    G = solve(Zx.T, Z[ns:, :ns].T).T
    H = solve(Zx.T, (Zx@solve(T[:ns, :ns], S[:ns, :ns])).T).T
    if max(float(abs(G.imag).max()), float(abs(H.imag).max())) > 1e-8:
        raise ValueError("non-real Schur policy")
    G, H = G.real, H.real
    stack = np.vstack([np.eye(ns), G])
    residual = float(np.max(abs(F0@stack+F1@stack@H)))
    radius = float(np.max(abs(np.linalg.eigvals(H))))
    if residual > 1e-8 or radius >= 1-1e-8:
        raise ValueError("stochastic equilibrium policy failed equation or stability checks")
    diagnostics = dict(equilibrium_residual_max_abs=residual, steady_state_error=base_error, spectral_radius=radius,
        stable_roots=ns, state_projection_condition=condition, system_dimension=dim,
        distribution_rank=basis.rank, full_distribution_dimension=kernel.d.size-kernel.constraints.shape[1],
        approximation_order=1, stochastic_tail_solved=True, model=kernel.model,
        household_derivatives="analytic" if kernel.model == "one_asset" else "centered finite differences",
        scope="local rational-expectations equilibrium, not a global or second-order aggregate-risk solution")
    for array in (G, H, F0, F1):
        array.flags.writeable = False
    return StochasticHANKPolicy(basis, H, G, float(rho), float(shock_std), diagnostics, kernel, F0, F1)


def solve_hank_stochastic_tree(policy: StochasticHANKPolicy, tree: pd.DataFrame, *,
                               tolerance: float = 1e-8, max_iterations: int = 30,
                               initial: np.ndarray | None = None, method: str = "krylov",
                               preconditioner: str = "sparse",
                               max_workspace_bytes: int = 1_073_741_824) -> HANKStochasticTreeResult:
    """Solve nonlinear finite histories with an endogenous stochastic terminal policy."""
    from ._hank_stochastic_tree import _solve_tree
    return _solve_tree(policy, tree, tolerance=tolerance, max_iterations=max_iterations,
                       initial=initial, method=method, preconditioner=preconditioner,
                       max_workspace_bytes=max_workspace_bytes)
